clue.text: The appropriate club for a wild clubman

definitions.text: The appropriate club for a wild clubman

parts.words: The appropriate club for a wild clubman
parts.note: the ... Club is a London gentlemen's club, and its name is also an adjective for someone wild and untamed, so a wild man belongs there

explanation.surface: Someone asks which London club suits an unruly member.
explanation.walkthrough: The London club of this name is a real gentlemen's club in Whitehall; its name also describes a fierce, uncivilised person.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means fierce or untamed, and it is also the name of a well-known London club.

clue.text: It is suggestive of immorality peculiar to our era

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, labels dates in the present era
vice is wickedness or immoral conduct

explanation.surface: Something suggestive is said to be a vice unique to modern times.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel offered to someone is a suggestion of what they should do.

clue.text: The purpose of a calendar which is standing up

definitions.text: The purpose of a calendar which is standing up

parts.words: The purpose of a calendar which is standing up
parts.note: a calendar exists so you can keep track of appointments; yet the same letters split differently describe neglecting a romantic engagement, which leaves the other person stood up

explanation.surface: A wall calendar propped upright on a desk and what it is for.
explanation.walkthrough: Split one way the phrase is what a calendar is for (to get the date); read as one word it is failing to turn up for a romantic meeting, which is 'standing up' your partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Missing an arranged romantic meeting is what being stood up amounts to, while a calendar's job is supplying today's day.

clue.text: Sea grave, it is said, tragically ended his speedboat career

indicators.note: the phrase tells us the words before it are to be pronounced, giving a surname with the same sound

parts.note: a grave at sea, a watery death, spoken as one surname

explanation.surface: A watery death, people say, brought a racer's speedboat career to a tragic end.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Segrave, British land and water speed record holder, was killed in 1930 on Windermere, England, when his speedboat Miss England II overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: The British record-breaker died in a 1930 speedboat crash on Windermere, ending his racing life.

clue.text: Coach senior staff on the art of working behind the scenes

definitions.text: the art of working behind the scenes

parts.note: a stagecoach, or stage, is a horse-drawn coach
the senior staff of a company are its management

explanation.surface: Training top executives in how to operate discreetly out of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a verb meaning train, but it is the noun: an old stagecoach, called a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a theatre production backstage is the craft carried out unseen by the audience.

clue.text: Mother breaks tablet under a plate

indicators.note: the word tablet is broken open so that another piece can sit inside it

parts.note: MA is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother drops a pill, which shatters beneath a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' puts MA inside TABLET, between its E and final T.
explanation.definitionFit: This protective mat sits on the dining table beneath a dish or plate to guard the surface from heat.

clue.text: Iron pots smashed in an atom smasher

definitions.note: describes the particle by where it turns up, in a particle accelerator

indicators.note: pots that are smashed are broken up, so the letters of iron pots are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cooking pots made of iron get wrecked inside a particle accelerator.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names a place where the particle is found: positively charged antielectrons are produced in particle accelerators.
explanation.definitionFit: This antiparticle of the electron is generated in particle accelerators, the machines nicknamed atom smashers.

clue.text: Aggregate of foundation members totally committed

definitions.meaning: broken brick and stone used as a base layer under roads and floors
the most dedicated, uncompromising inner group of supporters

explanation.definitionFit: The term covers both rubble laid beneath building foundations and the dedicated inner circle of a movement.

clue.text: Household brewer needs peat to brew

indicators.note: to brew is to mix and stew ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A homebrewer needs a supply of peat for making beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brew' rearranges PEAT and TO; 'needs' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This pot is where tea is brewed in the home, making it a domestic brewing vessel.

clue.text: Travel to a former Portuguese colony

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A traveller heads for one of Portugal's old colonial possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian state was ruled by Portugal until 1961.

clue.text: Dawdle to some degree just to avoid work

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree
to linger is to dawdle or delay

explanation.surface: Someone dawdles a little just to get out of doing any work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some degree' looks like the phrase meaning 'partly', but it supplies MA, a university degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To shirk duty, often by pretending illness, is to dodge one's job.

clue.text: Breather that is needed by a Highland hunter

parts.note: a gill is the organ a fish breathes with
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A Scottish hunter needs a pause for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' suggests a rest, but it is the fish's breathing organ.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland this is an attendant who helps on hunting, shooting or fishing trips.

clue.text: Enter memo it very satisfactory substitute!

definitions.text: Enter memo it very satisfactory substitute!

indicators.note: the letters of the first four words are swapped around to give a substitute arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to write a memo, with the remark that something else would serve far better.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the first four words rearranged give the answer, and a good recall is indeed a very satisfactory substitute for writing a memo.
explanation.definitionFit: A good recall that holds information well makes written reminders unnecessary.

clue.text: Draw announced after the draw

definitions.meaning: a game ending level, neither side winning
a cup match, whose pairings are announced once names are drawn

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a level result and a knockout fixture decided by lot.

clue.text: Illegally enter tame horse

definitions.meaning: to force entry into a building
to train a young horse to accept a rider

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both burglary and training a young horse.

clue.text: Peruse with reference to a Channel port

parts.note: re means concerning, with reference to
Dover is the English port on the Channel

explanation.surface: A traveller studies something about a harbour on the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is England's chief ferry port across the English Channel to France.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse something is to look through it, to scan the text again.

clue.text: A stupid fellow has to support Russian propaganda system

parts.note: git is British slang for a foolish or contemptible man
a prop is a support

explanation.surface: A fool is made to back the Soviet system of political messaging.
explanation.walkthrough: GIT is British slang for a stupid person; 'has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from the Soviet department for agitation and propaganda, so it names Russian political messaging.

clue.text: Second of this month

definitions.meaning: a moment, a very short time
an old commercial term for a date in the current month, as in 'the 5th inst.'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a moment, and in old business letters abbreviated inst. it denoted the current month.

clue.text: They may be classified as inclusive of date

indicators.note: the word as includes, or holds within it, the next piece

explanation.surface: Some documents could be secret, dates included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classified' suggests secret, but refers to small newspaper notices sorted by category.
explanation.definitionFit: Small newspaper notices are grouped by category in the classified section.

clue.text: A white usually thought of as yellow

definitions.text: A white usually thought of as yellow

parts.words: A white usually thought of as yellow
parts.note: ... white is a zinc-oxide artist's pigment, while the people of that nation were once crudely stereotyped as yellow

explanation.surface: A shade of white that most people would call yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Chinese white is a watercolour pigment; the clue plays on an old, now offensive, racial description of East Asians as 'yellow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese white is a white paint pigment, and the word for that nation's people was long linked with a yellow label.

clue.text: Dispiriting article lying about by hack writers

parts.note: laying about is a colloquial form of lying about, being idle
the is the definite article
ghosts are writers who produce work published under someone else's name

explanation.surface: A depressing newspaper piece left lying around by jobbing writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispiriting' looks like 'depressing' but means removing spirits, exorcising; ghostwriters are hack writers paid to write anonymously.
explanation.definitionFit: Exorcising is literally removing spirits, banishing phantoms from a haunted place.

clue.text: Ban rule governing dismissal

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A ban is imposed by the regulation covering sackings.
explanation.walkthrough: OUT is the cricket term for a dismissed batsman; 'governing' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: To prohibit something is to make it illegal, to forbid it.

clue.text: Wreath laid-for what?

indicators.note: a wreath laid out is arranged, so its letters are set down in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a wreath was placed at a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: Wreaths are laid at war memorials on Remembrance Sunday, so the answer is the reason for the laying.
explanation.definitionFit: Remembrance wreaths are placed for those killed in conflict, answering what they honour.

clue.text: Took the pledge, but opened the champagne

definitions.meaning: pawned an item, a pledge being the article left with a pawnbroker
a cork coming out of a bottle with a bang

explanation.definitionFit: The verb is British slang for pawning, and also describes a cork bursting out of a bottle.

clue.text: Maybe all mind, but never mind

definitions.meaning: pure mind with no physical substance at all
an expression meaning it is of no importance

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means having no physical substance; as an idiom it says something is unimportant.

clue.text: Welcome return of Senora Peron

indicators.note: a return brings the name back the other way, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Eva Peron, Evita, was the wife of Argentine president Juan Peron

explanation.surface: A greeting for Argentina's famous first lady on her homecoming.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Latin word of greeting, meaning hail.

clue.text: Charge with battery and mutiny

definitions.meaning: read as ..., putting electrical volts in again

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an uprising, and split cryptically suggests recharging with volts.

clue.text: Got the order off the mail order presumably

definitions.meaning: goods ordered by post are written off for

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means dismissed, and also describes requesting goods by post.
